terms.gloss: a court of justice; the trial held in it
terms.comment: Properly the trial, and by extension the court that holds it (Lewis & Short). To take someone to court, in jūdicium vocāre (Cic. Balb. 64, Lewis & Short) or addūcere (Traupman 194).

terms.gloss: summon to court; with īre or ambulāre, go to court
terms.grammar: phrase: jūs, jūris n. (the court) with in and the accusative
evidence: Traupman 197: in jūs īre, to go on trial
terms.comment: The summons before the praetor that began a lawsuit; jūs here is the place where justice is given (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Liv. 26.22.3: ad tribūnal cōnsulis vēnit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The raised platform on which the magistrate sat to give judgment; Morgan–Owens gives it for a court.
The colonnaded hall in the forum where courts sat and business was done, such as the basilica Jūlia (Lewis & Short); Traupman’s word for a courthouse.

phrases.latin: At ille in jūdicium vēnit, nihil eōrum negāvit, quae adversāriī crīminī dabant
phrases.english: But he came into court, and denied none of the things his opponents charged him with

phrases.latin: rapit in jūs; clāmor utrimque, undique concursus
phrases.english: he hauls him off to court; shouting on both sides, people running up from everywhere

sources: Lewis & Short: judicium · Lewis & Short: jus · Lewis & Short: tribunal · Lewis & Short: basilica
